html:
Damel, or king, of Cayor, the largest Wolof kingdom, who fought French expansion in Senegal off and on from the 1860s until he was killed in battle at Dekhele on 27 October 1886.

He made and broke treaties with the French, and opposed above all the railway from Dakar to Saint-Louis through his land, rightly seeing that it would end Cayor's independence. The line opened in 1885 and the French removed him. He had become a Muslim and was linked to the circle of Amadou Bamba, whose following grew after his death. He is a hero of Senegalese resistance, and his horse Malaw is famous in song. See also the Wolof states.
sum: Damel, or king, of Cayor, the largest Wolof kingdom, who fought French expansion in Senegal off and on from the 1860s until he was killed in battle at Dekhele on 27 October 1886.
